blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Sign language generation (SLG) maps written sentences into signing motion while preserving both lexical content and fine-grained articulation. This requires a model to decide what signs should be expressed and to realize them through precise handshape, trajectory, facial expression and body coordination. Existing pose-based systems and reconstruction-only motion tokenizers often entangle these two decisions, leaving the generator without an explicit text-aligned intermediate target for what to sign before refining how to sign it. To address this issue, we introduce Semantic Residual Vector Quantization (SRVQ), a framework for SLG that frames generation as a two-level process moving from semantics to kinematics. The newly introduced SRV Quantizer learns a hierarchy in which the first residual level encodes sign content and subsequent levels refine pose, handshape, trajectory, and body coordination, all within a single quantizer and without separate semantic representations or external planning stages. Through word-aware conditioning for hierarchical code generation, a masked semantic generator predicts semantic codes and a kinematic generator completes the residual codes for full SMPL-X motion synthesis. We evaluate using retrieval and FID in a shared text-motion embedding space, alongside standard geometric metrics. On CSL-Daily and Phoenix-2014T, SRVQ achieves R@1 of 82.3 and 70.3, outperforming the previous SOTA by 30 and 46 points, respectively.
blocks.zh: 手语生成(SLG)将句子写成签名动作,同时保留词汇内容和精细的表达. 这需要一种模型来决定应该表达什么迹象,并通过精确的手巾、轨迹、面部表情和身体协调来实现这些迹象。 现有的基于假构的系统和只重建的运动指示器经常缠绕这两个决定,使生成器在完善如何签字之前没有明确的文本对齐的中间目标来表示要签什么. 为了解决这一问题,我们引入了语义残余矢量量化(SRVQ),这是SLG的框架,它将生成设定为从语义向动因学转变的两级过程. 新引入的SRV量子学习了一种等级,其中第一个残余级编码是签名内容,随后的等级细化了姿势,手帕,轨迹,和机体协调,都在一个单一的量子内,没有单独的语义表述或外部规划阶段. 通过分级代码生成的文字感知调节,一个遮盖语义生成器预测语义编码,一个动能生成器完成SMPL-X运动全合成的剩余代码. 我们用一个共享的文本运动嵌入空间进行检索和FID评估,同时进行标准几何测量。 在CSL-Daily和Phoenix-2014T上,SRVQ实现82.3和70.3的R@1,分别比之前的SOTA成绩高30和46分.

blocks.en: Sign language is the primary language of many deaf and hard-of-hearing people, yet today’s digital society remains overwhelmingly built around spoken and written language [ 27 , 12 ] . As a result, deaf users are often pushed toward text-based interaction rather than being supported in their native sign language. Sign language generation (SLG) aims to bridge this access gap by mapping written-language sentences into continuous signing motion, enabling more inclusive and accessible interaction.
blocks.zh: 手语是许多聋人和听力困难的人的主要语言,然而,今天的数字社会仍然以口头和书面语言为主[27、12]。 因此,聋人用户往往被推向基于文字的交互,而不是用他们本土的手语支持. 手语生成(SLG)旨在通过将书面语句映射成连续的签名动作来弥补这一访问缺口,从而能够进行更具包容性和可获取性的互动.

blocks.en:
SLG poses two coupled challenges: generating a signing sentence requires determining the linguistic content to express, i.e . , which signs should be produced and in what order, while realizing each sign through fine-grained articulatory patterns, including handshapes, movement, facial expression, and body coordination. This makes SLG a two-level generation problem, entangling semantic sign selection with precise motion realization.
Yet, current models do not explicitly account for this two-level structure. They either generate signing motion end-to-end, mapping text directly to continuous poses [ 33 , 32 , 34 ] , leverage discrete motion tokens optimized for reconstruction-only [ 44 , 39 , 51 ] , or assume fixed intermediate sign representations that constrain the generation [ 50 ] .
As a result, semantic sign selection and motion realization are modeled within a shared representation, making it difficult to learn representations tailored to their distinct roles.
blocks.zh:
SLG带来了两个并存的挑战:生成签名句要求确定表达语言内容,即:哪些标志应该产生,以何种顺序产生,同时通过细纹的动脉模式实现每个标志,包括手巾,动作,面部表情,以及身体协调. 这使得SLG成为了两级生成问题,将语义符号选择与精确的运动实现包围起来.
然而,目前的模型并没有明确地说明这种两级结构。 它们要么生成签名运动端对端,将文本直接映射到连续的姿势[33,32,34],利用优化后仅用于重建的离散运动符号[44,39,51],要么假设固定的中间标志表示,限制生成[50].
因此,语义符号选择和运动实现都是在共同代表制中模式化的,因此很难学习适合其独特作用的表述.

blocks.en:
Latent image generation [ 41 , 5 ] and text-to-motion models [ 47 , 19 , 14 ] suggest a broader principle: complex generation benefits from intermediate token spaces, where high-level content can be organized before low-level details are synthesized.
Recent models in these domains introduce semantic structure by learning reasoning tokens on top of pretrained motion tokenizers [ 30 ] , separating semantic and pixel branches in unified image tokenizers [ 31 ] , or first learning a semantic codebook and then adding low-level refinement codebooks through staged training [ 7 ] .
These designs show the value of separating high-level semantics from low-level realization, but they usually require separate semantic spaces, staged training, or additional codebooks that are challenging to coordinate with reconstruction.
blocks.zh:
Latent图像生成[41,5]和文本对动模型[47,19,14]提出一个更广泛的原则:复杂的生成从中间符号空间中获益,在合成低层细节之前可以组织高层次的内容.
这些领域的近代模型通过在预先训练的运动指示器上方学习推理符号来引入语义结构[30],在统一的图像指示器中将语义分支和像素分支分开[31],或者首先学习一个语义代码本,然后通过舞台训练来添加低级的完善代码本[7].
这些设计显示了将高层次语义与低层次实现区分开来的价值,但是它们通常需要单独的语义空间,舞台训练,或者额外的代码本来与重建协调.

blocks.en:
To address these gaps, we propose Semantic Residual Vector Quantization (SRVQ) , a framework that formulates SMPL-X-based SLG in a semantic-to-kinematic fashion, explicitly reflecting the two-level structure of signing, as illustrated in Fig. 1 .
At the core of SRVQ, the SRV Quantizer employs a residual quantization hierarchy where the first residual codebook is semantically aligned through text and gloss supervision to capture what should be signed, while subsequent residual codebooks progressively encode the fine-grained kinematic details needed to realize it. All within the same quantizer hierarchy. Generation follows the same decomposition: a semantic generator predicts what to sign using word-aware conditioning that captures both global sentence and token-level lexical information, while a kinematic generator completes how the signs are articulated. We evaluate SRVQ on CSL-Daily [ 49 ] and Phoenix-2014T [ 21 ] using retrieval in a shared text-motion space, together with standard geometric distances. SRVQ achieves 82.3 R@1 on CSL-Daily and 70.3 on Phoenix-2014T, outperforming SOKE [ 51 ] by 30 and 46 points. Our contributions are summarized as follows: • We introduce SRVQ, a semantic-to-kinematic generation framework that decomposes SLG into a two-level process that first predicts semantic information and then complement it with residual kinematics. • We present the SRV Quantizer, which encodes motion through a single residual hierarchy learned with both reconstruction and text-alignment objectives. The first-level codebook captures high-level semantics, while later residual levels encode fine-grained kinematic details. • We introduce word-aware conditioning, in which both generators cross-attend to word-token embeddings augmented with a global sentence token, giving motion tokens direct access to local lexical cues while retaining sentence-level context. • SRVQ achieves state-of-the-art performance in SLG as measured with both retrieval and geometric metrics.
blocks.zh:
为了弥补这些差距,我们提议将语义残留的病媒量化(SRVQ)作为框架,以语义化方式制定基于SMPL-X的SLG,明确反映签字的两级结构,如图1所示。
在SRVQ的核心,SRVQuantizer采用残余的量子化等级,即通过文本和光泽监督对第一个残余的代码本进行集成对齐,以捕捉应当签名的内容,而之后的剩余代码本则逐渐将实现它所需的细纹运动细节编码. 都在同一类的等级中 生成遵循相同的分解:一个语义生成器预言使用既能捕捉全局句子又能捕捉到符位语法信息的字形感知条件来签名什么,而一个动能生成器则能完成符号的表达方式. 我们在CSL-Daily[49]和Phoenix-2014T[21]上使用共享文本移动空间的检索以及标准的几何距离来评价SRVQ. blocks.en: 2 Related Work
blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en:
Sign Language Generation. SLG aims to synthesize continuous signing motion from text input, and prior work has explored several ways to bridge this linguistic-to-kinematic gap.
Progressive Transformers [ 33 ] directly regress skeletal motion from text, while adversarial multi-channel training [ 32 ] and motion-primitive modeling [ 34 ] improve continuous pose generation.
Other methods synthesize human appearance through 3D avatars or meshes [ 38 , 2 ] , while related controllable image-generation methods introduce explicit pose or appearance conditions [ 35 , 36 ] . Diffusion-based methods model signing motion directly [ 10 ] .
Recent discrete approaches introduce a motion vocabulary before generation.
T2S-GPT [ 44 ] uses dynamic vector quantization for autoregressive sign generation, SOKE [ 51 ] combines discrete sign tokens with retrieval-enhanced conditioning, and M3T [ 39 ] introduces discrete multi-modal motion tokens. Several of these systems additionally use gloss annotations as intermediate supervision [ 33 , 43 ] , where glosses provide word-like labels for individual sign units and serve as sign-level anchors between spoken-language text and signing motion.
These methods improve sequence modeling, but the tokenizer is usually trained mainly for motion reconstruction.
As a result, the discrete code space is not explicitly organized to separate sign content from kinematic realization.
This motivates us to look beyond SLG to tokenized text-to-image and motion generation, where discrete or latent representations bridge high-level content and low-level synthesis.
blocks.zh:
手语生成. SLG旨在从文本输入中合成连续的签名运动,之前的工作探索了几种方法来弥补这种语言学到皮肤学的空白.
进化变形器[33]直接将骨骼运动从文本中退后,而对抗性多通道训练[32]和运动原型[34]则改善连续的姿势生成.
其他方法通过3D阿凡达或meshes合成人类外观[38,2],而相关的可控图像生成方法引入了明显的姿势或外观条件[35,36]. 基于传播的方法模型直接签名运动 [10].
最近离散的方法在生成前引入了运动词汇.
T2S-GPT [44] 采用动态矢量化进行自动递归式符号生成,SOKE [51] 将离散式符号符号与检索增强式条件结合,M3T [39]引入离散式多式运动符号. 其中一些系统还另外使用光泽说明作为中间监督[33,43],其中光泽为单个签名单位提供类似文字的标签,并作为标语文本和签名动作之间的标志级锚.
这些方法改进了序列建模,但标致器通常主要用于运动重建.
因此,离散代码空间没有被明确组织起来,以区分签名内容和运动实现.
这促使我们超越SLG,把文字到图像和运动生成的象征化,使离散或潜伏的表达将高层次的内容和低层次的综合联系起来。

blocks.en:
Semantic Organization in Tokenized Generation. Vector quantization provides a discrete interface between continuous signals and sequence models [ 41 ] .
In text-to-image generation, masked and autoregressive token models predict visual tokens before decoding them into pixels [ 5 , 22 , 15 ] , suggesting that an intermediate token space can separate high-level content prediction from low-level synthesis.
Text-to-motion generation adopts a similar tokenized formulation for temporally extended human motion.
T2M-GPT [ 47 ] and MotionGPT [ 19 ] model motion as discrete token sequences, while later methods further explore semantic-to-kinematic separation through global-local attention [ 48 ] , text-aligned motion representations [ 26 ] , explicit planning and posture stages [ 24 , 37 ] , or reasoning and execution latents [ 30 ] .
These works indicate that generation benefits from exposing an intermediate semantic structure before producing detailed motion.
However, this semantic-reconstruction balance is often introduced through additional objectives, separate representations, or multi-stage generator designs [ 48 , 26 , 24 , 37 , 30 ] .
Residual quantization [ 22 , 46 , 8 , 14 ] offers a natural hierarchy of codebooks, where later levels progressively reduce the residual error left by earlier ones. In existing image, audio, and text-to-motion tokenizers, this hierarchy is mainly used to improve reconstruction fidelity or rate-distortion trade-offs. SRVQ instead uses the hierarchy as a semantic-to-kinematic interface for SLG, assigning the first residual level to text-aligned sign content and the later levels to kinematic refinement.
blocks.zh:
托肯化一代语义组织. 矢量量化提供了连续信号和序列模型之间的离散接口[41].
在文本到图像生成中,蒙面和自递式的符号模型在解码成像素[5,22,15]之前会预测视觉符号,暗示中间的符号空间可以将高层次的内容预测与低层次的合成分开.
文本到运动生成采用类似的标注式配体,用于暂时延长人类运动.
T2M-GPT [47] 和 MotionGPT [19] 模型运动作为离散的符号序列,而后来的方法则通过全球-局部关注[48],文本对齐运动表述[26],明确的规划和姿态阶段[24,37],或推理和执行潜伏[30],进一步探索语义对亲切的分离.
这些作品表明,在产生详细运动之前,暴露中间语义结构,可以产生生成的好处.
然而,这种语义-重建平衡往往是通过附加目标,单独表述,或多阶段生成器设计[48,26,24,37,30]引入的.
残余量化[22,46,8,14]提供了编码本的自然等级,以后的等级逐渐减少早先的等级留下的残余错误. 在现有图像,音频,以及文本对移动的标注器中,这种等级制度主要用于改善重建忠心度或率扭曲权衡. SRVQ转而使用阶梯作为SLG的语义对等界面,将第一个剩余级指定为文本对齐的标志内容,而后一个级指定为动画精炼.

blocks.en:
Text Conditioning for Sign Generation. Beyond the tokenizer, the text representation used by the generator also matters.
Many SLG systems inherit the text-to-motion practice of conditioning generation on a pooled sentence embedding or a small set of global text tokens [ 40 , 23 , 44 , 51 ] .
This design gives the generator sentence-level context, but it can hide the local correspondences between words and sign segments.
The limitation is especially important for SLG because individual lexical units often determine handshape, spatial location, handedness, and local motion timing.
Our generator instead predicts semantic motion codes by cross-attending to word-token embeddings augmented with a global sentence token.
This exposes local lexical cues to every generated motion token while retaining sentence-level context for the whole sequence.
blocks.zh:
签名生成的文本条件 。 除了表示器外,生成器所使用的文本表示也很重要。
许多SLG系统继承了在嵌入集合句或一小组全局文本符号[40,23,44,51]上设定生成条件的文字对动作惯例.
这种设计给生成器句级上下文,但可以隐藏词段和签名段之间的局部对应.
限制对于SLG特别重要,因为单个的词典单位往往决定手巾,空间位置,手性,以及局部运动时间.
相反,我们的生成器预测了语义运动代码, 其方法是通过一个全局的句子符号, 来交叉选择字形嵌入。
这在保留整个序列的句子级别上下文的同时,使每个生成的动作符号都暴露出本地的词典提示.

blocks.en: 3 Method
blocks.zh: 3 方法

blocks.en: We introduce SRVQ, a semantic-to-kinematic framework for SLG, as shown in Fig. 2 . It first learns a SRV Quantizer ( Fig. 2 -top, Sec. 3.1 ) that decomposes signing motion into a text-aligned semantic level and residual kinematic levels. Later, in the Word-Aware Conditioning for Hierarchical Code Generation ( Fig. 2 -bottom, Sec. 3.2 ), we train a semantic generator to predict semantic codes ( Q 0 Q_{0} ) from text, while a kinematic generator completes the residual codes ( Q 1 Q_{1} – Q L Q_{L} ) required for full motion synthesis.
blocks.zh: 如图2所示,我们引入了SRVQ,即SLG的语义对语义框架。 它首先学习了一种SRV Quantizer(图2-top, Sec. 3.1),将签名运动分解为文本对齐的语义级别和剩余动能级别. 后来,在"阶代码生成的Word-Aware Contition"(图2-下方,第3.2sec.)中,我们训练一个语义生成器从文本中预测语义编码(Q 0 0}),而一个运动生成器完成全运动合成所需的剩余编码(Q 1Q_{1}—Q LQ_{L}).

blocks.en:
Problem Formulation. Given an input sentence 𝐜 = ( c 1 , … , c M ) \mathbf{c}=(c_{1},\ldots,c_{M}) , where c i c_{i} denotes the i i -th word, SLG aims to generate a continuous SMPL-X signing motion sequence 𝐒 ∈ ℝ T × 133 \mathbf{S}\in\mathbb{R}^{T\times 133} that preserves the sentence meaning.
Following [ 51 ] , we represent 𝐒 \mathbf{S} using a 133-dimensional SMPL-X parameterization and decompose it into body (including facial features), left-hand, and right-hand streams, denoted by 𝐒 B \mathbf{S}^{B} , 𝐒 L \mathbf{S}^{L} , and 𝐒 R \mathbf{S}^{R} .
We first describe how the SRV Quantizer learns a motion vocabulary whose first code level is aligned with sign content, and then introduce the hierarchical generators that predict semantic and residual codes from text.

继[51],我们代表S\mathbf{S}使用133维的SMPL-X参数化,将其分解为身体(包括面部特征),左手,右手流,由S B\mathbf{S}^{B},S L\mathbf{S}^{L}和S R\mathbf{S}^{R}表示.
我们首先描述了SRV Quantizer如何学习一个运动词汇,其第一个代码级别与符号内容一致,然后引入从文本中预测语义和剩余代码的层次生成器.

blocks.en:
Residual Vector Quantization (RVQ) [ 46 , 8 ] provides a natural mechanism for learning hierarchical discrete representations. We exploit this structure to separate semantics, i.e . , what to sign, from kinematic refinement, i.e . , how to sign it, within a single end-to-end quantizer, without imposing explicit constraints on how modeling capacity is allocated across levels. Specifically, the first residual level is trained as a text-aligned semantic codebook, capturing the meaning of the sign content to be produced, while the subsequent levels encode residual motion details that specify how the sign is articulated.
This design keeps semantic code prediction and motion reconstruction within the same hierarchy, providing the generator with an explicit semantic target while subsequent levels capture fine-grained motion details.

残余矢量量化(RVQ)[46,8]为学习分级离散表示提供了自然机制. 我们利用这个结构来将语义学,即什么是签名,从动能的修饰,即如何在单一的端对端的量子中签名,而不对建模能力如何在各个级别之间分配施加明确的限制. 具体地说,第一个剩余关卡被训练为文本对齐的语义编码本,捕捉要制作的标志内容的含义,而后续关卡则编码了指定标志如何表达的剩余运动细节.
这种设计将语义代码预测和运动重建保留在同一等级内,为生成者提供了明确的语义目标,而后续的关卡则捕捉精细的运动细节.

Inference. As shown in Fig. 3 -bottom, at inference time, a lightweight MLP first predicts the target token length T ′ T^{\prime} from the global sentence embedding 𝐞 sent \mathbf{e}_{\mathrm{sent}} . The length predictor is trained with cross-entropy over discretized length bins, using the

Given the predicted length, the semantic generator starts from a fully masked sequence of length T ′ T^{\prime} , to progressively decode semantic codes using confidence-based unmasking [ 5 ] . The resulting semantic codes are then passed to the kinematic generator, which predicts the residual codes needed to recover fine-grained articulatory details.

blocks.en: We evaluate SRVQ on standard sign language generation benchmarks. We first describe the evaluation protocol, including implementation details, datasets, and metrics. We then compare against prior work through both quantitative and qualitative evaluations, followed by ablation studies that isolate the contribution of the key design choices.

blocks.en: Datasets. We evaluate on CSL-Daily [ 49 ] (18K training / 1176 test sentences, Chinese sign language) and Phoenix-2014T [ 21 ] ( ∼ \sim 7K training / 642 test sentences, German sign language). Following prior work [ 51 ] , we use the released 133-dimensional SMPL-X pose annotations sampled at 25 fps. For gloss supervision, we rely on the frame-level annotations from Spoken2Sign [ 50 ] , which provide gloss labels together with their start and end frames.

blocks.en:
Evaluation Metrics. Following prior works [ 33 , 51 ] , we report DTW-JPE and DTW-PA.
DTW first aligns generated and reference motions over time with dynamic time warping, which reduces the effect of length and speed mismatch.
DTW-JPE then computes the average joint position error over the aligned frame pairs.
DTW-PA additionally applies Procrustes alignment before computing the same joint error, so it discounts global translation, rotation, and scale differences.
Lower values indicate a smaller geometric distance to the reference motion and, therefore, better fidelity.
However, geometric metrics alone are insufficient for assessing semantic correctness. A sentence can be signed with valid variations in timing, coarticulation, and style, and imperfect spatiotemporal alignment further complicates reference-based evaluation. As a result, geometric distance to a single reference cannot fully capture whether the generated motion preserves the intended meaning. Recent SLG evaluation studies therefore advocate embedding-based semantic evaluation as a complement to pose-distance metrics [ 18 , 20 ] . Retrieval-based semantic matching is also widely used in text-to-motion generation [ 47 , 29 , 14 , 16 ] and has recently been adopted in sign-language generation [ 45 , 3 ] . We use retrieval metrics as our primary semantic indicator. To this end, a pretrained text-motion retrieval model [ 1 ] embeds generated motions and text into a shared space.
For each benchmark, this evaluator is trained on real SMPL-X motion-text pairs from the corresponding training split and is used for all generated and real motions.
We report motion-to-text R ​ @ ​ 1 R@1 , R ​ @ ​ 5 R@5 , R ​ @ ​ 10 R@10 , and FID.
We refer to the Supplementary A for additional validation using Meaningful Pose and back-translation evaluators adapted to SMPL-X motion.

blocks.en: 4.2 Main Results
blocks.zh: 4.2 主要成果

blocks.en: Baselines. We compare SRVQ against representative sign language generation baselines reported by SOKE [ 51 ] . These include Progressive Transformer (Prog. Trans.) [ 33 ] , which directly regresses continuous signing poses; Text2Mesh [ 38 ] , which leverages mesh-based generation; and discrete motion-token generation methods, namely T2S-GPT [ 44 ] and S-MotionGPT [ 19 ] (MotionGPT [ 19 ] adapted for sign language as evaluated by SOKE). To ensure comparability, we report geometric metrics using the numbers provided by SOKE [ 51 ] . Since prior work does not report retrieval-based metrics, we additionally evaluate SOKE under the same retrieval protocol used for SRVQ.
blocks.zh: 基线。 我们比较SRVQ与SOKE报告的代表性手语生成基线[51]. 其中包括进步变形器(Prog. Trans.)[33],它直接倒退了连续的签名姿势;Text2Mesh[38],它利用了基于网格的生成;以及离散的运动脚本生成方法,即T2S-GPT[44]和S-MotionGPT[19](SOKE评价后为手语改编的MotionGPT[19]). 为了确保可比性,我们使用SOKE提供的数字报告几何测量。 由于先前的工作不报告基于检索的度量衡,我们根据用于SRVQ的相同检索协议,额外评价SOKE.

blocks.en: Quantitative Results. Tab. 1 compares SRVQ with state-of-the-art SLG models. We report two variants: Semantic-only , which decodes motion after predicting only the level-0 semantic codes Q 0 Q_{0} , and sem+kinematic , which additionally predicts the residual kinematic codes before decoding.
blocks.zh: 量化结果。 Tab. 1将SRVQ与最先进的SLG模型进行比较. 我们报告两种变体:只有语义(semantic- only),在只预测了一级-0语义代码Q 0 0}后解码运动,还有sem+kinematic(英语:sem+kinematic),在解码前还额外预测了剩余语义代码.

blocks.en: SRVQ outperforms prior methods across nearly all considered metrics. Sem+kinematic achieves the strongest semantic retrieval performance on both datasets, while semantic-only performs best on most geometric metrics.
blocks.zh: SRVQ几乎在所有考虑的衡量标准中都超过了以往的方法。 Sem+kinematic在两个数据集上都实现了最强的语义检索性能,而只有语义在大多数几何度量上表现最好.

blocks.en:
Intuitively, semantic-only produces a coarse, temporally smooth, low-frequency representation that is close to the average of many valid articulations of the same sign, which is well aligned with what DTW-based metrics reward. We revisit this observation in Sec. 4.4 . In contrast, sem+kinematic adds articulation details, improving the model’s ability to capture fine-grained distinctions between samples. On CSL-Daily, sem+kinematic improves R@1 from 51.96 to 82.31, yielding a gain of 30.35 percentage points over the strongest prior baseline. On Phoenix-2014T, it improves R@1 from 24.14 to 70.25, a gain of 46.11 points, and also obtains the best FID.
Notably, most of the semantic retrieval gain already comes from explicit semantic modeling, supporting the proposed hierarchical semantic modelling.
Retrieval improvements are consistent across R@5 and R@10, indicating that the generated motions are not only ranked closer to the correct sentence at top-1, but also occupy a better neighborhood in the embedding space.
For reference, the retrieval R@1 of real test motions under the same protocol is 87.0 on CSL-Daily and 71.0 on Phoenix-2014T, showing that Sem+kinematic substantially closes the gap to ground-truth retrievability.

blocks.en:
Semantic Alignment. Tab. 2 examines the effect of semantic supervision on the quantizer. Results show that removing both text and gloss alignment ( λ text = 0 , λ gloss = 0 \lambda_{\text{text}}=0,\lambda_{\text{gloss}}=0 ) yields the worst performance across most metrics, highlighting the importance of injecting semantic information into the learned motion codes. Removing gloss supervision ( No-gloss ) still provides a moderate improvement over the unaligned variant, reaching sem+kinematic R@1 scores of 75.60 on CSL-Daily and 58.88 on Phoenix-2014T. The full objective further improves performance,( λ text = λ gloss = 0.1 \lambda_{\mathrm{text}}=\lambda_{\mathrm{gloss}}=0.1 ) raising generation to 82.31 on CSL-Daily and 70.25 on Phoenix-2014T.
Increasing to λ = 0.3 \lambda=0.3 does not consistently improve generation.
It lowers CSL-Daily R@1 to 80.78 while improving Phoenix-2014T R@1 to 74.92.
We use λ = 0.1 \lambda=0.1 by default, which provides a balanced trade-off between semantic alignment and motion reconstruction.

Lexical Organization of Semantic Codes. We further examine whether the learned semantic codes organize motions according to lexical content, comparing their latent structure with the reconstruction-only codes from SOKE [ 51 ] .
To this end, we select ten frequent glosses from CSL-Daily and extract the token features corresponding to their annotated gloss spans. We visualize the resulting representations with t-SNE [ 42 ] , color-coding samples by their associated gloss. Fig. 5 shows that our text-aligned tokenization form clearer lexical neighborhoods than the reconstruction-only VQ-VAE from SOKE [ 51 ] . This suggests that reconstruction-only tokenization does not explicitly encourage lexical organization, whereas our semantic alignment objective induces a motion code space that better reflects sign-level content.
The quantitative neighborhood statistics in Tab. 3 confirm the same trend. Our representation increases the nearest-neighbor same-keyword rate (NN) from 56.2% to 73.8%, improves both precision-at- K K metrics (P@ K K ), and raises the silhouette score (Sil.) from 0.032 to 0.260.
This confirms that semantic supervision shapes level-0 codes toward text-aligned generation.

blocks.en: Text Conditioning Design. Tab. 4 compares conditioning strategies for the full generation pipeline, namely the use of a global sentence embedding vs. the word-aware textual representation. Cross-attending both the global textual representation ( 𝐞 sent \mathbf{e}_{\mathrm{sent}} ) and the word ( 𝐖 \mathbf{W} ) consistently improves over global sentence conditioning alone, e.g . , 82.31 vs . 75.34 R@1 in CSL-Daily and 92.52 vs . 79.28 R@10 for Phoenix-2014T, showing the benefit of exposing lexical information to the generators. Notably, the gain is particularly large on Phoenix-2014T, with an approximately 29-point improvement in R@1. We hypothesize that this is due to the Phoenix-2014T’s narrow weather-forecast domain, where sentences share coarse semantics but differ in key lexical cues such as cold, rain, or winter. Thus, global sentence embeddings may fail to capture the exact signs required. In contrast, CSL-Daily’s broader everyday vocabulary offers greater sentence-level variation, where word-level lexical information have diminishing returns.
blocks.zh: 文字条件设计. 标签4比较了全生成管道的调节策略,即使用全局句子嵌入法与文字意识表达法. 交叉参考全球文本表述(e发送\mathbf{e}_{\mathrm{sent}}})和单词(W\mathbf{W})都持续改善了全球句子设定,例如,CSL-Daily的82.31 vs 75.34 R@1和凤凰-2014T的92.52 vs 79.28 R@10,显示了向生成者披露词汇信息的好处. 值得注意的是,凤凰城-2014T的增益特别大,R@1的增幅约为29分. 我们假设这是因为凤凰城-2014T的狭义天气预测域, 因此,全球句子嵌入可能无法捕捉到所需的确切迹象. 相比之下,CSL-Daily的更广泛的日常词汇提供了更大的句子级别差异,其中的词级词汇信息减少了回报.

Residual Levels. Tab. 5 investigates how many residual levels are needed for sign-motion quantization. We report retrieval metrics as the main comparison, since geometric metrics are less sensitive to the fine-grained kinematic details that are primarily encoded from level 1 onward. SRVQ remains robust when using fewer residual levels, with the number of residuals having a smaller impact on performance than the SRVQ semantic alignment and word-aware conditioning design. Training fewer residual generators does not consistently improve over the six-level model.
We refer to the Supplementary B for additional ablations.

blocks.en: 4.4 Analysis of the DTW–Retrieval Discrepancy

blocks.en:
We conduct a diagnostic prefix-truncation experiment on the same generated motions on full test set: for a kept prefix ratio r r , we evaluate only the first r r fraction of generated frames while leaving the reference motion and input text unchanged.
This truncation removes the latter part of the predicted signing sequence, and should therefore reduce generation quality because some sign content no longer exists.
As shown in Tab. 6 , retrieval and FID follow this expectation.
In contrast, DTW scores improve as the evaluated prefix becomes shorter.
This indicates that DTW reflects geometric alignment under temporal warping, which may not always track sentence-level semantic preservation.

blocks.en: 5 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 5 结论

blocks.en:
We presented SRVQ, an SLG framework built around a semantic residual quantization hierarchy in which the coarsest level is jointly trained with a semantic alignment objective.
This design creates a discrete semantic intermediate representation that bridges text and motion, enabling a two-level generation process within a single unified quantizer hierarchy, without separate semantic and reconstruction architectures.
Paired with word-aware conditioning for hierarchical code generation, SRVQ surpasses the state-of-the-art on CSL-Daily and Phoenix-2014T by large margins in retrieval quality while the semantic-only variant improves upon prior baselines on most geometric metrics.
blocks.zh:
我们提出了SRVQ,一个SLG框架,它围绕一个语义剩余量化等级体系构建,在这个体系中,最短的层次被以语义对齐目标联合培训.
这种设计创造了一个离散的语义中间代表,将文字和运动连接起来,使得一个统一的四分位结构内部能够有一个双层生成过程,没有单独的语义结构和重建结构.
具有分级代码生成的字词感知条件的Paire,SRVQ在CSL-Daily和Phoenix-2014T的检索质量上以很大的差值超过了最先进的水平,而唯语义的变体在大多数几何度量的先前基线上有所改进.

blocks.en:
Limitations. SRVQ still relies on high-quality SMPL-X motion annotations and frame-level gloss supervision during quantizer training, although no gloss annotations are required at inference.
Future work will study more cross-lingual settings, explicit modeling of non-manual markers, and will incorporate a Deaf-participant human study.

今后的工作将研究更多的跨语言环境,明确非手工标记的模型,并将纳入聋哑人参与的人类研究。

blocks.en: A.2 Meaningful Pose Evaluation
blocks.zh: A.2 有意义的Pose评价

blocks.en: We additionally evaluate our method using the Meaningful Pose toolkit [ 20 ] , which provides complementary pose-retrieval and reconstruction metrics over all joints, body, hands and face. Since the original toolkit does not directly support SMPL-X motion, we adapt it by converting SMPL-X sequences to OpenPose keypoints, resampling them to a fixed length, and performing geometry-only pose retrieval using L2 distance. Unlike the main text–motion retrieval, this is motion-to-motion retrieval: each generated pose sequence is directly compared with a gallery of ground-truth pose sequences using only resampled keypoint geometry. The low absolute R@1 values are therefore expected because retrieving the exact paired motion requires matching signer-, timing-, and articulation-specific geometry; they should not be numerically compared with the text–motion R@1, but only compared across methods under this same protocol. Table 9 reports results for the sem+kinematic and sem-only variants against SOKE, confirming the trends observed with the text–motion retrieval and geometric metrics in the main paper. Specifically, sem+kinematic achieves the strongest pose-retrieval performance on both datasets for all-joint and hand queries, while sem-only generally yields the best reconstruction. Sem+kinematic also improves over SOKE on Phoenix-2014T and achieves comparable or slightly lower reconstruction performance on CSL-Daily. No learned text–motion, back-translation model is involved in this evaluation.

Active is the fraction of codebook entries used by at least one valid token, Norm. perplexity is the code usage perplexity normalized by the codebook size, and Top-1 is the token fraction assigned to the most frequent code.

This indicates that SRVQ does not collapse to a few dominant codes.
The only low-activation case is body Q0 on Phoenix-2014T, which is expected for a constrained broadcast domain with limited body pose.
All higher body residual levels remain highly active, showing that the residual hierarchy is still used for kinematic detail.

blocks.en: Tab. 19 reports performance across different ground-truth motion lengths. For retrieval, only the queries are grouped by length, while the gallery remains the full test set, ensuring that retrieval difficulty is unchanged across groups. DTW increases steadily with motion length, whereas retrieval performance does not exhibit a monotonic trend. On Phoenix-2014T, the shortest sequences achieve the lowest DTW scores but the lowest R@1, suggesting that short weather-domain sentences are geometrically easier to align yet semantically more difficult to distinguish.
